description: Hostile-input corpus: X25519 public keys that BOTH implementations must reject. Unlike the other vector files, which pin agreement on valid inputs, this one pins agreement on rejection — the gap that let the low-order defect exist, where Go's curve25519.X25519 errored while Rust's x25519-dalek silently returned an all-zero shared secret. An exchange against any key below yields an all-zero shared secret, making every derived key publicly computable. Consumed by crypto/vectors_test.go (Go) and rust/src/crypto.rs + rust/src/detect.rs (Rust). Append-only.
reference: docs/spec.md 'Common Attack Vectors', Small-Order Key Registration; docs/planning/done/DONE_LOW_ORDER_KEY_VALIDATION_PLAN.md
source: libsodium has_small_order() table (crypto_scalarmult/curve25519/ref10). Five canonical u-encodings plus two non-canonical ones that reduce to small-order points; the non-canonical pair is why both implementations delegate to their curve library rather than comparing against a table.

reject.name: identity-all-zeros
reject.note: The only one the pre-fix chain rejected, and only because an explicit all-zeros check happened to exist.

reject.name: p-non-canonical-zero
reject.note: Reduces to 0 mod p. A hand-maintained blacklist has to remember this one; delegating to the curve library gets it for free.

accept.name: ordinary-public-key
accept.note: From encryption.json — a real derived public key. Guards against over-rejection: the check must never refuse an honest guardian.

accept.name: high-bit-set
accept.note: X25519 masks the high bit of the u-coordinate, so this must still be accepted — a naive byte comparison against the p-based entries above could wrongly reject values in this shape.
